newsitem.title: USA: Defect in male chromosome may cause infertility.
newsitem.headline: Defect in male chromosome may cause infertility.

text.p: Small defects in the male chromosome may be responsible for some cases of infertility, according to research by University of Minnesota doctors published in Thursday's New England Journal of Medicine.
Dr. Jon Pryor and his team found that 7 percent of the 200 infertile men they studied were missing tiny pieces of their Y chromosomes, small bits of genetic material found only in males.
However, further study revealed that the deleted pieces did not always cause infertility. Out of six infertile men with the deletions, two had fathers with the same defect.

Nonetheless, the Pryor team said the finding "furthers our ability to diagnose infertility, suggest assisted reproduction sooner, and save the couple money, time and heartache" if doctors can point to a reason for their inability to produce a child.
